newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India slides, waiting for SBI.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India slides, waiting for SBI.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) were weaker in light trade, with the main focus State Bank of India's forthcoming GDR issue.
"Most funds are sellers of choice, although they are holding on to their core stocks," said one trader.

The James Capel Indian GDR Index fell 0.67 points, or 0.98 percent to 67.99 points, a premium of 11.57 percent over the local market, after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index came off early highs to close 6.19 points up at 3,343.92.

SBI's new issue, which is expected to raise up to $400 million, is seen as being well received, not out of any new enthusiasm for India, but because it is such a large part of the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index.
The stock accounts for 7.9 percent of the BSE-30 index and is frequently the most actively traded stock on both the Bombay and National exchanges.
"People just have to have it if they are in India," said the trader.
Fundamentals for the bank are compelling, it is trading on 9.6 times prospective 1998 earnings compared with 14.2 times for its Asia peers.
The Capel Taiwan Index fell 0.2 points, 0.22 percent to 87.95 points, a premium of 2.65 percent over the local market after the Taiwan Weighted Index fell 39.33 points to 6,438.52.

The Capel Korea Index rose 2.99 points, 4.48 percent to 69.85 points, a premium of 28.92 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index added 15.3 points to 793.21. -- David Chance, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5887
